headline: Nvidia's Huang whiplash overshadows deeper AI debt and spending doubts
body: Equity markets are whipsawing around the Nvidia story rather than settling into a clear trend. Monday's board decision to reinstate Jensen Huang as CEO sent the stock roughly 30% higher in a single session, one of the largest one-day gains on record for a major US company, but the rally reversed by Tuesday as Nvidia and other AI-linked names fell back and dragged the Nasdaq down about 1.5% while the Dow held up better. That pattern has carried into today's session, with reports describing a renewed slide across Asian markets, including a sharp drop in Taiwan's benchmark, as doubts about the durability of the AI trade resurface. The S&P 500 remains well off its October 6 high, in the high single digits year-to-date drawdown terms, keeping the index closer to correction territory than it has been in months even without a confirmed clean break below that threshold.

Underneath the index-level chop, the more persistent worry looks financial rather than purely sentiment-driven: today's coverage points to growing unease over AI-related debt issuance and whether Big Tech's spending pace is outrunning free cash flow, a concern that predates this week's Huang-driven swings. That lines up with a recent Fed survey in which a large majority of market contacts named AI as a top financial-stability risk, up sharply from earlier this year. Retail behavior has leaned toward buying weakness rather than fleeing it, brokerage order-flow data from Nvidia's prior selloff this month showed buy orders running several times ahead of sell orders, though verified social-sentiment chatter specific to today was thin, so this read leans more on price action and news flow than on confirmed retail mood.
